classification.difficultyReason: Identify the exposed inside surfaces of an open cylinder, calculate paint coverage, and round the number of cans up.

content.prompt:
Jessica is repainting a swimming pool in the shape of a cylinder $1.5\text{ m}$ tall and $6\text{ m}$ in diameter.
The inside of the pool is to be repainted, including the floor.
If a one-litre can of paint covers $9\text{ m}^2$, find the number of cans needed.

spec.description: Unshaded upright cylindrical pool with an open elliptical top, vertical sides, visible front floor rim and dashed hidden rear floor rim. Height dimension is at the left; diameter dimension is below.
spec.mathematics: Diameter 6 m, radius 3 m, height 1.5 m. Paint the circular floor and curved inside wall; exclude the open top.

answer.worked:
The open top is excluded; paint the curved wall and circular floor.
$$\begin{align*}
r&=6\div2=3\text{ m}\\
A&=2\pi rh+\pi r^2\\
A&=2\pi(3)(1.5)+\pi(3)^2\\
A&=18\pi\text{ m}^2\approx56.5\text{ m}^2\\
\text{Paint required}&=\frac{18\pi}{9}=2\pi\text{ L}\approx6.3\text{ L}
\end{align*}$$
Round up to buy enough paint: $7$ one-litre cans.
